## D7 (2026-07): local review core, CLI parity, and no direct forge integration
8
9
**Decision.** Gander's core object is a durable local review session over
10
jj-visible changes. Users or external harnesses are responsible for fetching,
11
checking out, or otherwise preparing teammate/agent work in a workspace where
12
jj can see it. Gander reads that code state and writes review state: viewed
13
marks, comments, tasks, walkthroughs, and artifacts.
14
15
Gander should not directly integrate with GitHub/GitLab/SourceHut for now: no
16
PR fetching, no review posting, no forge-specific comment sync. Harnesses can
17
consume Gander artifacts/CLI output and post elsewhere if desired.
18
19
**Interface rule.** The CLI is the baseline automation contract. Every
20
capability exposed through MCP, the TUI, or a future web UI must have a
21
scriptable CLI equivalent, and all interfaces must call the same core business
22
logic. MCP remains valuable, but it is an optional adapter rather than the
23
privileged path; some users avoid MCP because tool definitions and state can
24
pollute agent context.
25
26
**Workspace rule.** Review-state operations must not mutate the user's code
27
workspace. Inspecting jj state is fine; fetching, rebasing, checking out,
28
editing files, committing, moving bookmarks, or posting remote reviews belongs
29
to explicit user/harness workflows outside the review-state core. Existing
30
confirmed jj helpers remain exceptional, user-confirmed affordances rather than
31
implicit session behavior.
32
33
**Supersedes/refines.** D5's phrasing that harnesses should "arrive via MCP".
34
MCP is still supported, but CLI parity is mandatory and direct forge
35
integration is out of scope for the current product direction. See

docs/vision.md and roadmap milestones 11-16.

class="ln">41</td><td><pre>gander review create --revset @</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">42</td><td><pre>gander tui</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">43</td><td><pre>```</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">44</td><td><pre></pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">45</td><td><pre>External harnesses can fetch code, run agents, post review comments, create</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">46</td><td><pre>issues, or edit files. Gander provides the structured review artifact and the</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">47</td><td><pre>local commands/protocols those harnesses can consume.</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">48</td><td><pre></pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">49</td><td><pre>## Design rules</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">50</td><td><pre></pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">51</td><td><pre>1. **Local-first and forge-agnostic.** Review sessions are rooted in the local</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">52</td><td><pre>   jj repository/workspace, not in GitHub/GitLab/etc. Hosting-provider</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">53</td><td><pre>   integrations belong in harnesses or wrappers until a later explicit product</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">54</td><td><pre>   decision changes that boundary.</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">55</td><td><pre>2. **Do not mutate the user&#39;s code workspace.** Inspect jj state freely and</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">56</td><td><pre>   persist Gander state, but do not fetch, checkout, rebase, commit, edit files,</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">57</td><td><pre>   or move bookmarks as a side effect of reviewing. Any helper that would run a</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">58</td><td><pre>   jj mutation must be explicit, confirmed, and outside the review-state core.</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">59</td><td><pre>3. **Core first; interfaces are adapters.** TUI, CLI, MCP, and future web UI</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">60</td><td><pre>   must call the same review-domain services. No interface gets separate</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">61</td><td><pre>   business logic.</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">62</td><td><pre>4. **CLI parity is mandatory.** Every capability exposed through MCP or the TUI</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">63</td><td><pre>   must have a scriptable CLI equivalent, preferably with stable `--json`</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">64</td><td><pre>   output. Many agent workflows should work without MCP to avoid context</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">65</td><td><pre>   pollution.</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">66</td><td><pre>5. **MCP is optional, not privileged.** MCP is a convenience adapter for</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">67</td><td><pre>   harnesses that want typed tools. It should be thin over the same core API and</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">68</td><td><pre>   no more capable than the CLI.</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">69</td><td><pre>6. **Durable review sessions are the core product object.** A diff is input;</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">70</td><td><pre>   the durable session is the thing Gander creates, resumes, exports, and shares</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">71</td><td><pre>   with agents.</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">72</td><td><pre>7. **Private thinking precedes publishing.** Comments, tasks, and walkthroughs</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">73</td><td><pre>   are local/private until an external tool exports or posts them. Gander should</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">74</td><td><pre>   make review intent explicit but not surprise users by publishing anything.</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">75</td><td><pre></pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">76</td><td><pre>## Review session model</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">77</td><td><pre></pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">78</td><td><pre>The next-generation review session should include:</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">79</td><td><pre></pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">80</td><td><pre>- subject: jj pointing at files/hunks/ranges/symbols with</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">86</td><td><pre>  explanations and rationale;</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">87</td><td><pre>- exports in JSON, Markdown, and eventually static HTML.</pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">88</td><td><pre></pre></td></tr><tr class="add"><td class="ln"></td><td class="ln">89</td><td><pre>This model is the shared substrate for self-review, reviewing   <header class="hero"><p class="eyebrow">Take the tour</p><h1>gander turns jj diffs into durable, guided, actionable review sessions for humans and agents.</h1><p class="lede">Review locally, keep your state, leave action-tagged comments, guide readers through intent, and export a shareable artifact without handing your workflow to a forge.</p><div class="actions"><a class="button primary" href="index.html">Install / download</a><a class="button" href="https://git.sr.ht/~averagechris/gander">Source repository</a></div></header>
21
  <section><h2>Watch it in motion</h2><div class="demo"><img src="demo.gif" alt="Animated demo of gander reviewing a jj change in the terminal UI"></div></section>
22
  <section><h2>At a glance</h2><div class="grid">
23
    <article class="card"><h3>Review sessions</h3><p>Durable viewed-state, comments, tasks, and walkthroughs survive across TUI, CLI, and agent turns.</p></article>
24
    <article class="card"><h3>Guided walkthroughs</h3><p>Author steps with <span class="badge">Y</span>, open the panel with <span class="badge">W</span>, then tour in zen mode with <span class="badge">T</span>/<span class="badge">Z</span>.</p></article>
25
    <article class="card"><h3>Action-tagged comments &amp; tasks</h3><p>Cycle actions with <span class="badge">a</span>/<span class="badge">K</span>, triage work in the <span class="badge">X</span> tasks popup, and make review feedback executable.</p></article>
26
    <article class="card"><h3>Agent collaboration</h3><p>MCP tools mirror the CLI, and <span class="badge">@</span> summons an agent into the same local review context.</p></article>
27
    <article class="card"><h3>Scriptable CLI</h3><p>Reviews, comments, tasks, walkthroughs, files, and hunks all have JSON-friendly commands.</p></article>
28
    <article class="card"><h3>Shareable HTML exports</h3><p><code>gander export html</code> renders a self-contained dark review page ready to hand to a teammate.</p></article>
29
  </div></section>

    <article class="flow"><h3><span class="num">01</span> Self-review before sharing</h3><p>Create a review, mark files viewed, and leave yourself notes while intent is fresh.</p><pre><code>gander reviews create --title &quot;Self-review parser cleanup&quot;

# Roadmap
22
3
This project should become a fast, local-first review cockpit for jj changes,
4
and eventually a collaborative one: agents should be able to help conduct the
5
review, not just watch it (see milestones 7-9 and docs/decisions.md for the
6
directional decisions behind them).
3
This project should become a fast, local-first review workspace for jj-visible
4
changes: humans and agents use durable review sessions to understand, annotate,
5
walk through, and act on code changes. See [docs/vision.md](vision.md) for the
6
north star, non-goals, and post-MVP milestone plan.
77
88
## Product principles
99
1010
- **Speed first.** Startup should feel instant on normal changes. Generated or huge files must be easy to hide or collapse.
1111
- **Review state is durable but conservative.** A file is considered viewed only if the current diff fingerprint matches the saved fingerprint.
1212
- **Local artifacts are first-class.** JSON is for agents/tools; Markdown is for humans in Slack/email/docs.
13
- **Gander reads code state and writes review state.** Users or external
14
  harnesses prepare/fetch work; Gander inspects jj state and persists review
15
  sessions, comments, tasks, and walkthroughs without mutating the code
16

docs/vision.md
added+169-0
@@ -0,0 +1,169 @@
1
# Product vision
2
3
Gander's north star is to be a **local-first review workspace for jj-visible
4
changes**: the place where humans and agents jointly understand, annotate,
5
walk through, and act on code changes without Gander owning remote-provider or
6
working-copy orchestration.
7
8
In one sentence:
9
10
> Gander turns jj diffs into durable, guided, actionable review sessions for
11
> humans and agents.
12
13
## What Gander owns
14
15
Gander should read code state and write review state.
16
17
It owns:
18
19
- reading jj changes, revsets, files, hunks, symbols, and diff context;
20
- durable review sessions, viewed state, comments, tasks, walkthroughs, and
21
  exported artifacts;
22
- local review navigation in the TUI and future web/static views;
23
- machine-readable automation through a complete CLI surface and optional MCP
24
  adapter;
25
- safe handoff points where external human or agent harnesses can decide what
26
  to do next.
27
28
It should not own:
29
30
- fetching pull requests or remote branches;
31
- posting reviews to GitHub/GitLab/SourceHut or other forges;
32
- rebasing, checking out, editing, committing, or otherwise mutating code as
33
  part of review state management;
34
- a general-purpose agent chat UI;
35
- MCP as the only automation path.
36
37
The expected integration model is that a user or harness prepares a workspace
38
where the work is already visible to jj, then invokes Gander there:
39
40
```sh
41
gander review create --revset @
42
gander tui
43
```
44
45
External harnesses can fetch code, run agents, post review comments, create
46
issues, or edit files. Gander provides the structured review artifact and the
47
local commands/protocols those harnesses can consume.
48
49
## Design rules
50
51
1. **Local-first and forge-agnostic.** Review sessions are rooted in the local
52
   jj repository/workspace, not in GitHub/GitLab/etc. Hosting-provider
53
   integrations belong in harnesses or wrappers until a later explicit product
54
   decision changes that boundary.
55
2. **Do not mutate the user's code workspace.** Inspect jj state freely and
56
   persist Gander state, but do not fetch, checkout, rebase, commit, edit files,
57
   or move bookmarks as a side effect of reviewing. Any helper that would run a
58
   jj mutation must be explicit, confirmed, and outside the review-state core.
59
3. **Core first; interfaces are adapters.** TUI, CLI, MCP, and future web UI
60
   must call the same review-domain services. No interface gets separate
61
   business logic.
62
4. **CLI parity is mandatory.** Every capability exposed through MCP or the TUI
63
   must have a scriptable CLI equivalent, preferably with stable `--json`
64
   output. Many agent workflows should work without MCP to avoid context
65
   pollution.
66
5. **MCP is optional, not privileged.** MCP is a convenience adapter for
67
   harnesses that want typed tools. It should be thin over the same core API and
68
   no more capable than the CLI.
69
6. **Durable review sessions are the core product object.** A diff is input;
70
   the durable session is the thing Gander creates, resumes, exports, and shares
71
   with agents.
72
7. **Private thinking precedes publishing.** Comments, tasks, and walkthroughs
73
   are local/private until an external tool exports or posts them. Gander should
74
   make review intent explicit but not surprise users by publishing anything.
75
76
## Review session model
77
78
The next-generation review session should include:
79
80
- subject: jj revset/change stack/base+tip already visible in the workspace;
81
- files, hunks, stable anchors, fingerprints, viewed state, and symbols;
82
- comments with kind, status, action intent, author, timestamps, and target;
83
- tasks derived from comments or created directly, such as `explain`,
84
  `research`, `fix`, `write-tests`, `document`, or `export`;
85
- walkthroughs: ordered steps pointing at files/hunks/ranges/symbols with
86
  explanations and rationale;
87
- exports in JSON, Markdown, and eventually static HTML.
88
89
This model is the shared substrate for self-review, reviewing agent-generated
90
changes, onboarding new contributors, and collaborative teammate review.
91
92
## Milestone plan
93
94
### M11: Core review sessions
95
96
- Promote sessions to first-class durable objects.
97
- Model comments, action-tagged tasks, walkthrough steps, and stable targets in
98
  the domain layer.
99
- Keep artifacts serializable and migratable.
100
- Preserve existing viewed-state/comment behavior through the new model.
101
102
### M12: Complete CLI surface
103
104
- Add scriptable commands for sessions, files, hunks, comments, tasks,
105
  walkthroughs, and exports.
106
- Ensure mutating review-state commands write only Gander state.
107
- Provide stable `--json` output for harnesses and agents.
108
- Treat the CLI as the automation contract, not just a human convenience.
109
110
Example shape:
111
112
```sh
113
gander reviews list --json
114
gander reviews show <id> --json
115
gander hunks list --review <id> --file src/lib.rs --json
116
gander comments add --review <id> --hunk <hunk-id> --kind issue --action fix
117
gander tasks list --review <id> --status open --json
118
gander walkthrough add-hunk --review <id> --hunk <hunk-id> --why "Entry point"
119
gander walkthrough export --review <id> --format markdown
120
```
121
122
### M13: TUI over the session core
123
124
- Make the TUI read and write the same session objects as the CLI.
125
- Add first-class affordances for key hunks, walkthrough editing, action-tagged
126
  comments, and open review tasks.
127
- Keep focused/zen review modes as presentations of walkthrough/session state.
128
129
### M14: MCP parity adapter
130
131
- Rework MCP tools as thin wrappers over the same services used by the CLI.
132
- Keep the current live-instance routing and `current_focus` value where useful.
133
- Document the CLI equivalent for every MCP tool.
134
135
### M15: Static web walkthroughs
136
137
- Export a self-contained HTML review/walkthrough artifact for sharing or
138
  onboarding.
139
- Include key hunks, comments, task state, and walkthrough navigation.
140
- Keep it local/static first; no hosted sync or forge integration.
141
142
### M16: Optional local web UI
143
144
- Add an interactive local browser UI only after the session model stabilizes.
145
- Use the same core services and respect the no-code-mutation boundary.
146
147
## Canonical workflows
148
149
### Self-review
150
151
```sh
152
gander review create --revset @
153
gander tui
154
gander tasks list --status open --json
155
gander walkthrough export --format markdown
156
```
157
158
### Reviewing an agent's changes
159
160
An external agent edits code in a jj workspace. Gander inspects the resulting
161
change, the human leaves action-tagged tasks, and the agent harness consumes
162
those tasks through CLI or MCP. The agent may edit files; Gander only records
163
and resolves review state.
164
165
### Reviewing teammate changes
166
167
A user or harness fetches/checks out/prepares the teammate change. Gander opens
168
against the local jj-visible revset. Any posting to a remote review system is a
169
separate harness concern using Gander's exported comments/artifacts.

pub fn ensure_session<'a>(
48
    state: &'a mut ReviewState,
49
    target: &SessionTargetSpec,
50
    title: Option<&str>,
51
) -> &'a mut ReviewSession {
52
    if let Some(index) = state.sessions.iter().position(|session| {
53
        session.status == ReviewSessionStatus::Open && target_matches(&session.target, target)
54
    }) {
55
        return &mut state.sessions[index];
56
    }
57
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
58
    state.sessions.push(ReviewSession {
59
        id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
60
        title: title.map(str::to_owned),
61
        target: ReviewTarget {
62
            repo: target.repo.clone(),
63
            base: target.base.clone(),
64
            revision: target.revision.clone(),
65
            revset: target.revset.clone(),
66
            ..ReviewTarget::default()
67
        },
68
        status: ReviewSessionStatus::Open,
69
        created_at: Some(now),
70
        updated_at: Some(now),
71
        ..ReviewSession::default()
72
    });
73
    state.sessions.last_mut().unwrap()
74
}

pub fn find_session<'a>(state: &'a ReviewState, prefix: &str) -> Result<&'a ReviewSession> {
98
    let matches = state
99
        .sessions
100
        .iter()
101
        .filter(|session| session.id.starts_with(prefix))
102
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
103
    match matches.as_slice() {
104
        [session] => Ok(session),
105
        [] => Err(eyre!("unknown review session `{prefix}`")),
106
        _ => Err(eyre!("ambiguous review session prefix `{prefix}`")),
107
    }
108
}

#[allow(dead_code)]
111
pub fn find_session_mut<'a>(
112
    state: &'a mut ReviewState,
113
    prefix: &str,
114
) -> Result<&'a mut ReviewSession> {
115
    let matches = state
116
        .sessions
117
        .iter()
118
        .enumerate()
119
        .filter(|(_, session)| session.id.starts_with(prefix))
120
        .map(|(index, _)| index)
121
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
122
    match matches.as_slice() {
123
        [index] => Ok(&mut state.sessions[*index]),
124
        [] => Err(eyre!("unknown review session `{prefix}`")),
125
        _ => Err(eyre!("ambiguous review session prefix `{prefix}`")),
126
    }
127
}

pub fn add_walkthrough_step(session: &mut ReviewSession, step: WalkthroughStep) -> WalkthroughStep {

    if session.walkthroughs.is_empty() {
279
        session.walkthroughs.push(Walkthrough {

            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
281
            title: Some("Walkthrough".to_owned()),

            steps: Vec::new(),
283
        });
284
    }

    let mut step = step;

    if step.id.is_empty() {

        step.id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
288

pub fn remove_walkthrough_step(
295
    session: &mut ReviewSession,
296
    step_id: &str,
297
) -> Result<WalkthroughStep> {
298
    for walkthrough in &mut session.walkthroughs {
299
        if let Some(index) = walkthrough
300
            .steps
301
            .iter()
302
            .position(|step| step.id.starts_with(step_id))
303
        {
304
            let step = walkthrough.steps.remove(index);
305
            touch(session);
306
            return Ok(step);
307
        }
308
    }

    Err(eyre!("unknown walkthrough step `{step_id}`"))

pub fn move_walkthrough_step(
313
    session: &mut ReviewSession,

    step_id: &str,
315
    new_index: usize,
316
) -> Result<WalkthroughStep> {
317
    for walkthrough in &mut session.walkthroughs {
318
        if let Some(index) = walkthrough
319
            .steps
320
            .iter()
321
            .position(|step| step.id.starts_with(step_id))
322
        {
323
            let step = walkthrough.steps.remove(index);
324
            let to = new_index.min(walkthrough.steps.len());
325
            walkthrough.steps.insert(to, step.clone());
326
            touch(session);
327
            return Ok(step);
328
        }
329
    }
330
    Err(eyre!("unknown walkthrough step `{step_id}`"))

}

//! Review-task overlay: actionable comments for human/agent handoff.
2
3
use crate::{app::ReviewSession, state::CommentState};
4
5
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
6
pub(super) struct TaskListState {
7
    /// Comment ids matching the actionable task filter, in comment order.
8
    pub(super) comment_ids: Vec<String>,
9
    pub(super) selected: usize,
10
}
11
12
impl TaskListState {
13
    pub(super) fn new(session: &ReviewSession) -> Self {
14
        let mut state = Self {
15
            comment_ids: actionable_comment_ids(session),
16
            selected: 0,
17
        };
18
        state.clamp(session);
19
        state
20
    }
21
22
    pub(super) fn refresh(&mut self, session: &ReviewSession) {
23
        let selected_id = self.selected_comment_id().map(str::to_owned);
24
        self.comment_ids = actionable_comment_ids(session);
25
        if let Some(id) = selected_id
26
            && let Some(index) = self
27
                .comment_ids
28
                .iter()
29
                .position(|candidate| candidate == &id)
30
        {
31
            self.selected = index;
32
        }
33
        self.clamp(session);
34
    }
35
36
    pub(super) fn clamp(&mut self, _session: &ReviewSession) {
37
        self.selected = self.selected.min(self.comment_ids.len().saturating_sub(1));
38
    }
39
40
    pub(super) fn move_selection(&mut self, delta: isize) {
41
        if self.comment_ids.is_empty() {
42
            self.selected = 0;
43
            return;
44
        }
45
        let max = self.comment_ids.len() as isize - 1;
46
        self.selected = (self.selected as isize + delta).clamp(0, max) as usize;
47
    }
48
49
    pub(super) fn selected_comment_id(&self) -> Option<&str> {
50
        self.comment_ids.get(self.selected).map(String::as_str)
51
    }
52
}

fn actionable_comment_ids(session: &ReviewSession) -> Vec<String> {
55
    session
56
        .comments
57
        .iter()
58
        .filter(|comment| {
59
            comment.state == CommentState::Todo
60
                || comment.action.is_some_and(|action| !action.is_none())
61
        })
62
        .map(|comment| comment.id.clone())
63
        .collect()
64
}

73
    }

}

5
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
6

18

    }

22

28
        }
29

30
    }
31
32
    pub(super) fn move_selection(&mut self, delta: isize) {
33

34
            self.selected = 0;
35
            return;
36
        }
37
        let max = self.step_ids.len() as isize - 1;

fn walkthrough_step_ids(session: &ReviewSession) -> Vec<String> {

54

            durable.status == ReviewSessionStatus::Open
56

}

use crate::state::{ReviewState, ReviewTarget, Walkthrough, WalkthroughStep};
2
3
/// Render persisted local walkthroughs as Markdown.
4
///
5
/// This intentionally reads only Gander review state: no server, forge
6
/// metadata, agent overlay, or working-copy mutation. Agent/zen concepts can be
7
/// mapped into persisted walkthroughs by a later reconciliation layer.
8
pub fn render_walkthroughs_markdown(state: &ReviewState) -> String {
9
    let walkthroughs = state
10
        .sessions
11
        .iter()
12
        .flat_map(|session| session.walkthroughs.iter())
13
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
14
15
    if walkthroughs.is_empty() {
16
        return "# Walkthroughs\n\nNo walkthrough steps recorded.\n".to_owned();
17
    }
18
19
    let mut out = String::from("# Walkthroughs\n\n");
20
    for (index, walkthrough) in walkthroughs.iter().enumerate() {
21
        if index > 0 {
22
            out.push('\n');
23
        }
24
        write_walkthrough(&mut out, walkthrough);
25
    }
26
    out
27
}
28
29
fn write_walkthrough(out: &mut String, walkthrough: &Walkthrough) {
30
    let title = walkthrough
31
        .title
32
        .as_deref()
33
        .map(str::trim)
34
        .filter(|title| !title.is_empty())
35
        .unwrap_or("Untitled walkthrough");
36
    out.push_str("## ");
37
    out.push_str(title);
38
    out.push_str("\n\n");
39
40
    if walkthrough.steps.is_empty() {
41
        out.push_str("No steps recorded.\n");
42
        return;
43
    }
44
45
    for (index, step) in walkthrough.steps.iter().enumerate() {
46
        write_step(out, index + 1, step);
47
    }
48
}
49
50
fn write_step(out: &mut String, number: usize, step: &WalkthroughStep) {
51
    let title = step
52
        .title
53
        .as_deref()
54
        .map(str::trim)
55
        .filter(|title| !title.is_empty())
56
        .unwrap_or_else(|| step.id.trim());
57
    out.push_str(&format!("### {number}. {title}\n\n"));
58
59
    if let Some(location) = target_location(&step.target) {
60
        out.push_str(&format!("Location: `{location}`\n\n"));
61
    }
62
63
    if let Some(why) = step
64
        .why
65
        .as_deref()
66
        .map(str::trim)
67
        .filter(|why| !why.is_empty())
68
    {
69
        out.push_str("Why: ");
70
        out.push_str(why);
71
        out.push_str("\n\n");
72
    }
73
74
    if let Some(body) = step
75
        .body
76
        .as_deref()
77
        .map(str::trim)
78
        .filter(|body| !body.is_empty())
79
    {
80
        out.push_str(body);
81
        out.push_str("\n\n");
82
    }
83
}
84
85
fn target_location(target: &ReviewTarget) -> Option<String> {
86
    let file = target.file.as_deref()?;
87
    let mut location = match (target.line, target.end_line) {
88
        (Some(start), Some(end)) if end != start => format!("{file}:{start}-{end}"),
89
        (Some(line), _) => format!("{file}:{line}"),
90
        _ => file.to_owned(),
91
    };
92
    if let Some(symbol) = target
93
        .symbol
94
        .as_deref()
95
        .map(str::trim)
96
        .filter(|symbol| !symbol.is_empty())
97
    {
98
        location.push_str(" — ");
99
        location.push_str(symbol);
100
    }
101
    Some(location)
102
}

        out.push_str("<a class=\"file-link\" href=\"#");

    for file in &session.files {

        let comments: Vec<_> = state

        out.push_str("<section class=\"card file\" id=\"");

        out.push_str("</span><span class=\"stat add\">+");

        out.push_str("</span><span class=\"stat del\">-");

                    DiffLineKind::Meta => "meta",

fn line_range(line: Option<usize>, end_line: Option<usize>) -> String {

    match (line, end_line) {
206
        (Some(a), Some(b)) if a != b => format!("{a}-{b}"),
207
        (Some(a), _) => a.to_string(),
208
        _ => String::new(),
209
    }
210

fn file_anchor(path: &str) -> String {
219
    let mut anchor = String::from("file-");
220
    for b in path.bytes() {
221
        if b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
222
            anchor.push(b as char);
223
        } else {
224
            anchor.push('-');
225
        }
226
    }
227
    anchor
228
}

fn esc_to(out: &mut String, text: &str) {
231
    for ch in text.chars() {
232
        match ch {
233
            '&' => out.push_str("&amp;"),
234
            '<' => out.push_str("&lt;"),
235
            '>' => out.push_str("&gt;"),
236
            '"' => out.push_str("&quot;"),
237
            '\'' => out.push_str("&#39;"),
238
            _ => out.push(ch),
239
        }
240
    }
241
}
